newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Wall Street fuels Singapore stocks' rally at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street fuels Singapore stocks' rally at open.

text.p: The Singapore stock market rose early Tuesday boosted by overnight gains on Wall Street, dealers said.

"Our market is firmer because of the U.S. strength and rebound after the market digested what Greenspan had said," a dealer said, referring to the Federal Reserve chairman's anti-inflationary speech last Thursday.
"But volume is low. Most markets in Asia will remain cautious," he added.
At 0200 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 14.51 points at 2,211.64.
Turnover was light around 16.4 million with gainers leading losers by 145 to 24.
Dealers said foreign buying underpinned blue chips, mainly the foreign tranches of banks like DBS, OCBC and UOB.

Multimedia company Creative was lifted by the strong performance in Nasdaq overnight. Creative led gainers, rising Singapore $1.30 (US$0.93) to S$13.50. The SES electronic index soared over 3.0 percent to 89.51.
Informatics was active with 1.2 million shares traded, of which 300,000 were crossed at S$0.59. It was up S$0.02 at S$0.63.
